methane.title: Methane
methane.alt: Displayed structure of Methane. Every carbon has four bonds. This is a flat displayed formula, not the molecule’s three-dimensional shape.
methane.caption: Every carbon has four bonds. This is a flat displayed formula, not the molecule’s three-dimensional shape.

ethane.title: Ethane
ethane.alt: Displayed structure of Ethane. Every carbon has four bonds. This is a flat displayed formula, not the molecule’s three-dimensional shape.
ethane.caption: Every carbon has four bonds. This is a flat displayed formula, not the molecule’s three-dimensional shape.

propane.title: Propane
propane.alt: Displayed structure of Propane. Every carbon has four bonds. This is a flat displayed formula, not the molecule’s three-dimensional shape.
propane.caption: Every carbon has four bonds. This is a flat displayed formula, not the molecule’s three-dimensional shape.

butane.title: Butane
butane.alt: Displayed structure of Butane. Every carbon has four bonds. This is a flat displayed formula, not the molecule’s three-dimensional shape.
butane.caption: Every carbon has four bonds. This is a flat displayed formula, not the molecule’s three-dimensional shape.

pentane.title: Pentane
pentane.alt: Displayed structure of Pentane. Every carbon has four bonds. This is a flat displayed formula, not the molecule’s three-dimensional shape.
pentane.caption: Every carbon has four bonds. This is a flat displayed formula, not the molecule’s three-dimensional shape.

hexane.title: Hexane
hexane.alt: Displayed structure of Hexane. Every carbon has four bonds. This is a flat displayed formula, not the molecule’s three-dimensional shape. Hexane is included as a useful extension beyond the named five-carbon alkane drawing requirement.
hexane.caption: Every carbon has four bonds. This is a flat displayed formula, not the molecule’s three-dimensional shape. Hexane is included as a useful extension beyond the named five-carbon alkane drawing requirement.

ethene.title: Ethene
ethene.alt: Displayed structure of Ethene. The two parallel lines are a carbon–carbon double bond. Count the bonds at each carbon before adding hydrogen.
ethene.caption: The two parallel lines are a carbon–carbon double bond. Count the bonds at each carbon before adding hydrogen.

propene.title: Propene
propene.alt: Displayed structure of Propene. The two parallel lines are a carbon–carbon double bond. Count the bonds at each carbon before adding hydrogen.
propene.caption: The two parallel lines are a carbon–carbon double bond. Count the bonds at each carbon before adding hydrogen.

but-1-ene.title: But-1-ene
but-1-ene.alt: Displayed structure of But-1-ene. The two parallel lines are a carbon–carbon double bond. Count the bonds at each carbon before adding hydrogen.
but-1-ene.caption: The two parallel lines are a carbon–carbon double bond. Count the bonds at each carbon before adding hydrogen.

but-2-ene.title: But-2-ene
but-2-ene.alt: Displayed structure of But-2-ene. The two parallel lines are a carbon–carbon double bond. Count the bonds at each carbon before adding hydrogen.
but-2-ene.caption: The two parallel lines are a carbon–carbon double bond. Count the bonds at each carbon before adding hydrogen.

methylpropane.title: Methylpropane
methylpropane.alt: Displayed structure of Methylpropane. The branch changes atom connections. Compare this with the straight chain of butane.
methylpropane.caption: The branch changes atom connections. Compare this with the straight chain of butane.

ethanol.title: Ethanol
ethanol.alt: Displayed structure of Ethanol. The oxygen bonds to carbon and hydrogen. The C–O–H group is the alcohol functional group.
ethanol.caption: The oxygen bonds to carbon and hydrogen. The C–O–H group is the alcohol functional group.

ethanoic-acid.title: Ethanoic acid
ethanoic-acid.alt: Displayed structure of Ethanoic acid. The carboxyl carbon belongs to the main chain: this acid has two carbon atoms, not one.
ethanoic-acid.caption: The carboxyl carbon belongs to the main chain: this acid has two carbon atoms, not one.

ethyl-ethanoate.title: Ethyl ethanoate
ethyl-ethanoate.alt: Displayed structure of Ethyl ethanoate. The C(=O)–O linkage joins the acid-derived and alcohol-derived parts. No O–H bond remains in this ester.
ethyl-ethanoate.caption: The C(=O)–O linkage joins the acid-derived and alcohol-derived parts. No O–H bond remains in this ester.

dibromoethane.title: 1,2-dibromoethane
dibromoethane.alt: Displayed structure of 1,2-dibromoethane. Bromine adds across the former C=C. One Br attaches to each carbon; no hydrogen is displaced.
dibromoethane.caption: Bromine adds across the former C=C. One Br attaches to each carbon; no hydrogen is displaced.

cracking.title: Cracking a long-chain alkane
cracking.alt: A labelled sequence: C10H22, then Heat + catalyst, then C8H18 + C2H4.
cracking.caption: One balanced example: ten carbon atoms and twenty-two hydrogen atoms occur on each side. Product mixtures can vary.

ethanol-routes.title: Fermentation route to ethanol
ethanol-routes.alt: A labelled sequence: Glucose solution, then Yeast, no oxygen, then Ethanol + CO2.
ethanol-routes.caption: Fermentation is a biological conversion. Hydration of ethene is a separate industrial route, explained in the notes.

esterification.title: Esterification
esterification.alt: A labelled sequence: Alcohol + acid, then Acid catalyst, then Ester + water.
esterification.caption: The reaction is reversible. Here “acid” on the left means a carboxylic acid; the catalyst is a separate condition.

fractionating-column.title: Fractional distillation of crude oil
fractionating-column.alt: A tower is hot at the bottom and cooler at the top, with shorter-chain fractions leaving higher up.
fractionating-column.caption: Schematic, not apparatus to scale. Fractions have boiling ranges and contain mixtures of hydrocarbons.

elements.text: Heated crude enters near the base

combustion.title: Combustion products
combustion.alt: Two oxygen-supply conditions produce different products from a hydrocarbon fuel.
combustion.caption: Carbon monoxide and soot are possible products of incomplete combustion. Water can still form.

polymer-ethene.title: Poly(ethene) repeat unit
polymer-ethene.alt: A two-carbon single-bonded backbone with side groups preserved from the corresponding alkene.
polymer-ethene.caption: The bonds through the brackets continue into neighbouring repeat units. Restore C=C between these two backbone carbons to recover the monomer.

fraction-bars.title: Equivalent fractions
fraction-bars.alt: One strip has one half shaded; another has two quarters shaded, showing equal lengths.
fraction-bars.caption: Equal-sized wholes are essential: 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent because the shaded proportions match.

bounds-interval.title: Rounding and error intervals
bounds-interval.alt: A number line marks an inclusive lower bound 3.35 and exclusive upper bound 3.45 around 3.4.
bounds-interval.caption: A length of 3.4 cm to the nearest 0.1 cm represents 3.35 ≤ L < 3.45 cm. The upper endpoint rounds to 3.5.

quadratic-roots.title: Roots and the turning point
quadratic-roots.alt: A parabola y=x squared minus 4 crosses the x-axis at minus 2 and 2, with minimum at zero, minus 4.
quadratic-roots.caption: The graph is y = x² − 4. The roots solve x² − 4 = 0; the vertex is (0, −4).

inequality-line.title: A quadratic inequality on a number line
inequality-line.alt: The open interval between minus two and three is highlighted, with hollow endpoints.
inequality-line.caption: For (x + 2)(x − 3) < 0, choose −2 < x < 3. Test a value between the roots and values outside them.

linear-gradient.title: Gradient as rise over run
linear-gradient.alt: A line through (1,2) and (4,8) has a gradient triangle rising 6 while running 3.
linear-gradient.caption: Both coordinate changes must use the same direction: (8 − 2)/(4 − 1) = 2. Axes are schematic.

right-triangle.title: Choose sides from the chosen angle
right-triangle.alt: A right triangle labels the opposite side 3, adjacent side 4 and hypotenuse 5 relative to angle theta.
right-triangle.caption: Relative to the marked angle: sin θ = 3/5, cos θ = 4/5 and tan θ = 3/4. The drawing is not to scale.

circle-angle.title: Angle at the centre and circumference
circle-angle.alt: A circle shows a central angle AOB and an angle ACB subtended by the same chord AB on the major arc.
circle-angle.caption: The centre angle subtending the same minor arc AB is twice the angle at C on the major arc. Diagram not to scale.

vector-route.title: Vector routes between points
vector-route.alt: A directed triangle shows AB equals a, BC equals b and AC equals a plus b.
vector-route.caption: Following A to B to C gives the same displacement as A directly to C. Reversing an arrow changes the sign.

probability-tree.title: A tree without replacement
probability-tree.alt: A bag has two red and one blue counter. The first and second draw branches show changing probabilities.
probability-tree.caption: Multiply along a complete path. Add disjoint paths for an event such as one red and one blue.

histogram-density.title: Area, width and frequency
histogram-density.alt: Two histogram bars have unequal widths. Their areas represent frequencies, so height is frequency density.
histogram-density.caption: Example: 10–20 has frequency 12 and density 1.2; 20–40 has frequency 18 and density 0.9. Bars have unequal widths.

plant-animal-cells.title: Plant and animal cell comparison
plant-animal-cells.alt: A plant cell has a wall, membrane, vacuole, nucleus and chloroplasts; an animal cell has membrane and nucleus.
plant-animal-cells.caption: Simplified sections, not to scale. Both cell types also contain cytoplasm, mitochondria and ribosomes.

osmosis-membrane.title: Osmosis through a partially permeable membrane
osmosis-membrane.alt: Water can cross the central membrane. Larger solute particles remain on their side.
osmosis-membrane.caption: Net movement of water is from the more dilute side to the more concentrated side, under these conditions.

enzyme-temperature.title: Temperature and enzyme activity
enzyme-temperature.alt: An enzyme activity curve rises to an optimum and then falls steeply as denaturation increases.
enzyme-temperature.caption: Schematic: the optimum depends on the enzyme and conditions. Low temperature slows collisions; it does not normally denature an enzyme.

alveolus.title: Gas exchange at an alveolus
alveolus.alt: Air in an alveolus is next to a capillary, with oxygen diffusing into blood and carbon dioxide in the opposite direction.
alveolus.caption: Thin exchange surfaces, large area, ventilation and blood flow help maintain diffusion. Not to scale.

elements.text: Alveolar wall and capillary wall are each one cell thick.

heart-circulation.title: Double circulation
heart-circulation.alt: Four heart chambers connect lungs and body in two loops; arrows show the flow sequence.
heart-circulation.caption: Anatomical right is drawn on the left. Valves enforce one-way flow; the diagram is a route map, not a realistic heart shape.

villus.title: A villus and its transport routes
villus.alt: A finger-like villus has a thin epithelium, blood capillary network and central lacteal.
villus.caption: Glucose and amino acids enter the blood; products of fat digestion are transported through the lacteal after processing in the cells. Not to scale.

leaf-section.title: A leaf in section
leaf-section.alt: A cut through a leaf shows upper epidermis, palisade cells, spongy mesophyll with air spaces and a lower epidermis with a stoma.
leaf-section.caption: The palisade layer contains many chloroplasts. Air spaces connect the exchange surfaces to stomata. Simplified and not to scale.

reflex-arc.title: A spinal reflex route
reflex-arc.alt: Receptor to sensory neurone to relay neurone to motor neurone to effector, with synapses in the spinal cord.
reflex-arc.caption: Information also reaches the brain. A fast spinal reflex can begin before conscious awareness; the brain is not required to initiate this pathway.

nephron.title: Filtration and selective reabsorption
nephron.alt: A glomerulus inside Bowman’s capsule leads to a tubule and collecting duct; useful substances return to blood.
nephron.caption: The overview omits the detailed blood-vessel layout. Filtration occurs first; selective reabsorption changes the filtrate afterward.

elements.text: Useful substances and water can be reabsorbed.

punnett-labelled.title: An autosomal monohybrid cross
punnett-labelled.alt: A Punnett square for Tt by Tt has gametes T and t from each parent and offspring TT, Tt, Tt and tt.
punnett-labelled.caption: Each fertilisation is independent. A 3:1 phenotype ratio is an expected probability, not a guaranteed outcome for four offspring.

carbon-cycle.title: Carbon transfers between reservoirs
carbon-cycle.alt: Carbon moves from atmospheric carbon dioxide to plants, consumers and decomposers, and returns through respiration and combustion.
carbon-cycle.caption: Arrows show movement of carbon, not energy. Dead material also comes from plants and consumers.

distance-time.title: Distance-time: gradient is speed
distance-time.alt: A distance-time line is steep, then flat, then shallow.
distance-time.caption: A horizontal distance-time section means stationary. On a velocity-time graph a horizontal section would instead mean constant velocity.

velocity-time.title: Velocity-time: gradient and area
velocity-time.alt: A velocity-time line rises uniformly from zero then remains horizontal.
velocity-time.caption: Area under this positive velocity-time graph is displacement. Gradient gives acceleration; the flat section has zero acceleration.

force-diagram.title: Forces on a car
force-diagram.alt: A car has upward normal contact force, downward weight, forward driving force and backward resistive force.
force-diagram.caption: A free-body diagram shows forces acting on the car. Balanced vertical forces do not imply balanced horizontal forces.

lever-moment.title: Moments about a pivot
lever-moment.alt: A beam has a central pivot, a downward 20 N force 0.3 m left of it and a downward 10 N force 0.6 m right.
lever-moment.caption: For this horizontal beam, 20 × 0.3 = 10 × 0.6 = 6 N m. The distances are perpendicular distances from pivot to force lines.

parallel-circuit.title: Parallel branches
parallel-circuit.alt: Two resistors lie in separate branches connected to the same pair of supply nodes.
parallel-circuit.caption: Both resistors have the full supply potential difference. Conventional current splits at the junction and rejoins afterward.

refraction-normal.title: Refraction into glass
refraction-normal.alt: A ray from air enters a flat glass surface and bends towards the normal. Angles are measured to the normal.
refraction-normal.caption: The ray slows on entering glass; frequency stays constant and wavelength decreases. Not to scale.

converging-lens.title: A converging lens: real image
converging-lens.alt: An object beyond twice the focal length of a converging lens forms a real inverted smaller image between F and 2F on the far side.
converging-lens.caption: One ray travels parallel then through the far focus; one passes straight through the optical centre. Thin-lens schematic.

heating-curve.title: A heating curve
heating-curve.alt: Temperature rises in solid, is level during melting, rises in liquid, is level during boiling and rises in gas.
heating-curve.caption: Schematic for a pure substance at constant pressure. Energy is transferred throughout; plateaux do not mean heating has stopped.

half-life-graph.title: Exponential decay and half-life
half-life-graph.alt: Count rate after background subtraction falls from 80 to 40 to 20 over two equal half-life intervals.
half-life-graph.caption: Equal time intervals halve the expected corrected count rate; individual radioactive decays remain random.

electromagnetic-spectrum.title: Electromagnetic spectrum order
electromagnetic-spectrum.alt: The sequence is radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma. Wavelength decreases and frequency increases to the right.
electromagnetic-spectrum.caption: All travel at the same speed in vacuum. This is an ordered guide, not a frequency or wavelength scale.

transformer-coils.title: Transformer structure
transformer-coils.alt: Separate primary and secondary coils surround a shared iron core. Changing magnetic flux links the coils.
transformer-coils.caption: There is no direct electrical connection between the windings. A steady DC supply does not maintain transformer action.

binary-byte.title: An unsigned eight-bit byte
binary-byte.alt: The bits 10110100 align with place values 128,64,32,16,8,4,2,1, giving decimal 180.
binary-byte.caption: Each left shift of a place doubles its weight. A leading 1 is not automatically a minus sign in unsigned representation.

fetch-registers.title: Registers in the fetch phase
fetch-registers.alt: PC supplies the address to MAR, memory sends instruction to MDR, and MDR copies it to CIR while PC advances.
fetch-registers.caption: The arrows show logical transfers. MAR stores an address; MDR and CIR store data or instructions, not the same role.

binary-search.title: Binary search on a sorted list
binary-search.alt: A labelled sequence: Sorted list, then Check middle, then Discard half, then Repeat / stop.
binary-search.caption: If the target is absent, the remaining search interval becomes empty. The sorted order makes discarding half valid.

merge-sort.title: Merge sort: split then merge
merge-sort.alt: A list 7,2,5,1 splits into halves and singletons, then merges into sorted pairs and a sorted whole.
merge-sort.caption: The split stage does not sort. During each merge, compare the next unused element from each sorted input.

logic-gates.title: Boolean gate input-output map
logic-gates.alt: Inputs A and B feed AND and OR boxes, while A feeds a NOT box. Each output is labelled with its expression.
logic-gates.caption: Truth table rules: AND needs both true; OR needs at least one true; NOT reverses its single input. Boxes are functional symbols.

star-network.title: A wired star topology
star-network.alt: Four client devices each connect to a central switch with their own link.
star-network.caption: A cable failure usually affects one client link; a central switch failure affects devices depending on that switch.

web-request.title: From a name to a web page
web-request.alt: A labelled sequence: DNS finds IP, then Packets routed, then Server responds, then Browser renders.
web-request.caption: DNS resolves a domain name; it does not itself fetch the page. HTTPS uses encrypted communication.

image-pixels.title: Pixels and colour depth
image-pixels.alt: A four by four pixel grid uses four colours with a two-bit code for each colour.
image-pixels.caption: Four colours need at least two bits per pixel. This sixteen-pixel uncompressed image needs 32 bits of pixel data, excluding metadata.

sound-sampling.title: Sampling a sound wave
sound-sampling.alt: A smooth wave is sampled at regular time intervals; each sample is recorded at a finite amplitude level.
sound-sampling.caption: Sample rate controls the number of measurements per second. Bit depth controls the available amplitude codes. Schematic.

elements.text: Equal time gaps; finite amplitude precision

loop-flowchart.title: A count-controlled loop
loop-flowchart.alt: A flowchart initialises i to zero, tests i less than three, executes the body, increments i, and loops; false exits.
loop-flowchart.caption: Testing before the body gives iterations i = 0, 1 and 2. The first value failing i < 3 is 3.

timber-grain.title: Timber grain and plywood layers
timber-grain.alt: Solid timber fibres run mainly along one direction; plywood has adjacent veneers with perpendicular grain directions.
timber-grain.caption: Cross-lamination reduces directional movement and can improve dimensional stability. It does not make plywood waterproof without suitable grades and bonding.

mortise-tenon.title: Mortise and tenon: exploded assembly
mortise-tenon.alt: Isometric rail with a protruding tenon aligned to a rectangular mortise in a post, with shoulders and grain indication.
mortise-tenon.caption: Pictorial, not to scale. The shoulders seat against the post; the tenon fits the mortise. Fit, grain direction and adhesive area influence the joint.

elements.text: An accurately fitted joint needs room for adhesive without a loose, rocking fit.

vacuum-forming.title: Vacuum forming a softened sheet
vacuum-forming.alt: A heated thermoplastic sheet is drawn over a former on a perforated platen by a pressure difference.
vacuum-forming.caption: Air is removed below the sheet, so atmospheric pressure pushes it onto the former. Rounded corners and draft help release.

injection-moulding.title: Injection moulding: main parts
injection-moulding.alt: A hopper supplies granules to a heated barrel with a screw, which pushes molten polymer into a closed mould cavity.
injection-moulding.caption: A cooling stage solidifies the part before ejection. The diagram shows the process route, not machine guarding or operating instructions.

stress-strain.title: Elastic and plastic deformation
stress-strain.alt: A schematic load-extension curve begins with a straight elastic region and then bends into plastic deformation before fracture.
stress-strain.caption: The exact curve depends on material and specimen. Stiffness relates to resistance to elastic deformation; strength relates to load or stress before failure.

triangulation.title: Triangulating a frame
triangulation.alt: One rectangular frame has no diagonal and may rack into a parallelogram; another is braced diagonally.
triangulation.caption: A rigidly connected triangle resists changing shape without changing member lengths. Joint design and load direction still matter.

gear-pair.title: Meshing gears and speed ratio
gear-pair.alt: A small driver gear meshes with a larger driven gear. Their rotation directions are opposite.
gear-pair.caption: For 12 driver teeth and 36 driven teeth, the driven speed is one third of the driver speed. Teeth are represented schematically.

tolerance-fit.title: Clearance as a worst-case calculation
tolerance-fit.alt: A shaft has limits 9.8 to 10.0 mm, while a hole has limits 10.2 to 10.4 mm.
tolerance-fit.caption: Minimum clearance = smallest hole − largest shaft = 0.2 mm. Maximum clearance = largest hole − smallest shaft = 0.6 mm.

orthographic.title: First-angle orthographic arrangement
orthographic.alt: A front view is above the plan. The right-side view is placed to the left of the front view in first-angle projection.
orthographic.caption: The arrangement matters: first-angle and third-angle systems use different view positions. Dimensions and hidden detail must remain consistent.

design-cycle.title: Testing and improving a design
design-cycle.alt: A labelled sequence: User need, then Measurable spec, then Prototype test, then Justified change.
design-cycle.caption: A specification becomes useful when the test and pass criterion are defined. Actual project evidence must come from the student’s own work.

lifecycle.title: A product lifecycle
lifecycle.alt: A labelled sequence: Materials, then Manufacture, then Use / repair, then End of life.
lifecycle.caption: Transport can occur between stages. Evaluate the whole system rather than treating one recyclable material as proof of a low-impact product.

sodium-atom.title: Sodium: a shell-model atom
sodium-atom.alt: A sodium atom has eleven protons and an electron arrangement of 2,8,1. The nucleus is central and electrons occupy three schematic shells.
sodium-atom.caption: Not to scale or a literal electron orbit: the shell model represents electron arrangement. This example uses sodium-23 with twelve neutrons.

ionic-lattice.title: A sodium chloride lattice
ionic-lattice.alt: A regular two-dimensional slice alternates positive sodium and negative chloride ions.
ionic-lattice.caption: A small slice of a giant three-dimensional ionic lattice. Ionic attraction acts in all directions; NaCl does not consist of isolated Na–Cl molecules.

copper-electrolysis.title: Aqueous copper chloride with inert electrodes
copper-electrolysis.alt: Positive copper ions move to the negative cathode and form copper. Chloride ions move to the positive anode and form chlorine in the stated setup.
copper-electrolysis.caption: For a suitable aqueous copper(II) chloride solution and inert electrodes. Product predictions change with electrolyte, concentration and electrode material.

exothermic-profile.title: Energy profile: exothermic reaction
exothermic-profile.alt: Reactants lie at a higher energy than products. A peak shows activation energy and a lower alternative peak shows a catalysed pathway.
exothermic-profile.caption: Both pathways have the same reactant and product energies. A catalyst lowers activation energy, not the overall reaction energy change.

reaction-rate-curves.title: Rate and total product
reaction-rate-curves.alt: Two product-volume curves reach the same plateau; the faster reaction has a steeper initial gradient and levels off sooner.
reaction-rate-curves.caption: Same final product amount does not mean the same rate. This comparison assumes the same limiting amount and comparable collection conditions.

equilibrium-rates.title: Dynamic equilibrium: rates
equilibrium-rates.alt: Forward rate starts high and falls; reverse rate starts low and rises. They approach the same rate.
equilibrium-rates.caption: Equal rates at equilibrium do not mean equal reactant and product concentrations. Both reactions continue in a closed system.

titration-apparatus.title: Titration apparatus and readings
titration-apparatus.alt: A vertical burette delivers solution through a tap into a conical flask. Delivered volume is final reading minus initial reading.
titration-apparatus.caption: Read the meniscus at eye level and record the appropriate precision. Indicator and endpoint colour depend on the reaction and method.

chromatogram.title: Chromatography distances and Rf
chromatogram.alt: A paper chromatogram has a pencil baseline, a solvent front and separated spots. Distances are measured from the baseline.
chromatogram.caption: For the labelled spot, Rf = distance moved by spot / distance moved by solvent front. The baseline starts above the solvent level.

plant-transport.title: Xylem and phloem transport
plant-transport.alt: A plant diagram shows water moving upward in xylem and sugars travelling from a leaf source to shoot and root sinks in phloem.
plant-transport.caption: Xylem water flow is mainly root to shoot. Phloem translocation can occur in different directions in different sieve tubes, according to sources and sinks.

dna-protein.title: DNA to a protein
dna-protein.alt: A gene in DNA is transcribed to mRNA, which is translated at a ribosome into an amino-acid chain.
dna-protein.caption: The diagram is a process map, not a scale drawing. Base order determines codons and hence amino-acid sequence in the school model.

food-test-evidence.title: Food tests: observation and inference
food-test-evidence.alt: A table-like diagram matches iodine blue-black with starch, Benedict’s heated precipitate with reducing sugar, Biuret lilac with protein and an ethanol emulsion with lipid.
food-test-evidence.caption: Use approved supervised methods, controls and the actual observed result. Different tests use different reagents and conditions.

menstrual-cycle.title: Menstrual cycle: linked events
menstrual-cycle.alt: A schematic cycle links FSH to follicle development, an LH surge to ovulation, and progesterone to maintenance of the uterine lining.
menstrual-cycle.caption: Timing varies; the 28-day framework is a teaching model. The labels summarise roles and do not imply each hormone acts only at one instant.

elements.text: If no pregnancy: ovarian hormone levels

food-chain.title: Feeding relationships and energy transfer
food-chain.alt: A grass to rabbit to fox chain has arrows pointing from the food towards its consumer.
food-chain.caption: Arrows show energy transfer through feeding. Biomass and available energy decrease between trophic levels; energy is not recycled like carbon atoms.

pressure-depth.title: Liquid pressure and depth
pressure-depth.alt: Three points at increasing depth in a liquid have increasing gauge pressure. Pressure at the same depth is equal in a stationary uniform liquid.
pressure-depth.caption: Gauge pressure due to the liquid is p = hρg. Absolute pressure also includes pressure at the surface.

stellar-life.title: Stellar evolution paths
stellar-life.alt: A common nebula, protostar and main-sequence sequence branches into a Sun-like red-giant route and a massive-star supernova route.
stellar-life.caption: The final remnant depends on the star’s mass and mass loss. The two branches show different evolutionary routes, not a sequence every star follows.

motor-field.title: Force on a current-carrying conductor
motor-field.alt: A conductor carrying conventional current out of the page lies in a magnetic field left to right; the force is upward.
motor-field.caption: Field direction is N to S across the gap. A dot means current out of the page; reversing current or field reverses the force.

sql-table.title: Selecting rows and fields with SQL
sql-table.alt: An example table contains name and score fields; WHERE selects scores at least 60 and ORDER BY sorts the selected rows descending.
sql-table.caption: SELECT chooses fields; WHERE filters rows; ORDER BY arranges the result. These are different operations.

test-table.title: A purposeful input test
test-table.alt: A labelled sequence: Rule defined, then Normal / boundary, then Invalid input, then Expected outcome.
test-table.caption: A test records actual versus expected behaviour. Invalid data should be rejected or handled without damaging stored information.

thermal-treatment.title: Steel treatment choices
thermal-treatment.alt: A branching map distinguishes hardening by heating and rapid cooling from tempering that reduces brittleness after hardening.
thermal-treatment.caption: Exact temperatures and methods depend on the steel and approved workshop process. Hardness, toughness and strength are different properties.

design-loads.title: A justified material choice
design-loads.alt: A labelled sequence: Service load, then Needed property, then Material + process, then Test the product.
design-loads.caption: Hardness resists indentation; toughness resists fracture under impact. A useful justification names the property needed by the component.

non-right-triangle.title: A non-right triangle and opposite labels
non-right-triangle.alt: A triangle labels side a opposite angle A, side b opposite angle B and side c opposite angle C.
non-right-triangle.caption: The sine rule pairs each side with its opposite angle. The cosine rule uses the angle between the two sides in its product term. Not to scale.

simultaneous-intersection.title: A line meeting a quadratic
simultaneous-intersection.alt: The horizontal line y=1 meets y=x squared minus 3 at x=−2 and x=2.
simultaneous-intersection.caption: At each intersection the two y-values are equal, so x² − 3 = 1. The solutions are (−2, 1) and (2, 1).

halogen-displacement.title: Halogen displacement: electron transfer
halogen-displacement.alt: Chlorine gains electrons from bromide ions, producing chloride ions and bromine.
halogen-displacement.caption: Cl2 + 2Br− → 2Cl− + Br2. Chlorine is reduced and bromide is oxidised; electron counts match in the two half-equations.

elements.text: Chlorine displaces bromine from bromide solution

iv-apparatus.title: Measuring an I–V characteristic
iv-apparatus.alt: A cell, ammeter, variable resistor and test resistor are in series; a voltmeter is connected across the test resistor.
iv-apparatus.caption: Change potential difference using the approved low-voltage setup and record current. Keep the test component’s temperature controlled where required.

elements.text: A: current in series. V: potential difference across test component.

cyber-defence.title: Defences target different attack stages
cyber-defence.alt: A phishing message can lead to stolen credentials and unauthorised access; user training, authentication and access control target different stages.
cyber-defence.caption: Layered measures reduce different risks. No one control guarantees that every attack is prevented.

venn-sets.title: Two overlapping sets in a universal set
venn-sets.alt: A rectangle is the universal set. Circles A and B overlap in the intersection; the union includes both circles.
venn-sets.caption: A ∩ B contains items in both sets. A ∪ B contains items in either or both. A complement is taken relative to the universal set.

elements.text: Union = all regions inside either circle

polyester-repeat.title: A polyester repeat-unit example
polyester-repeat.alt: The backbone alternates diol-derived and diacid-derived groups with ester links. Carbonyl oxygens are shown above the backbone.
polyester-repeat.caption: Condensed repeat from ethane-1,2-diol and ethanedioic acid. Bonds extend through brackets; both acid carbons remain in the backbone.

elements.text: Ester links occur at C(=O)–O connections

methylbutane.title: 2-methylbutane
methylbutane.alt: Displayed structure of 2-methylbutane. Five carbons with a branch: this has the same molecular formula as pentane but different connections.
methylbutane.caption: Five carbons with a branch: this has the same molecular formula as pentane but different connections.

dimethylpropane.title: 2,2-dimethylpropane
dimethylpropane.alt: Displayed structure of 2,2-dimethylpropane. The central carbon bonds to four carbon neighbours and has no hydrogens. All three pentane isomers have C5H12.
dimethylpropane.caption: The central carbon bonds to four carbon neighbours and has no hydrogens. All three pentane isomers have C5H12.

methylpropene.title: 2-methylpropene
methylpropene.alt: Displayed structure of 2-methylpropene. A branched alkene with C4H8. Compare its connections with but-1-ene and but-2-ene; the central carbon has no hydrogen.
methylpropene.caption: A branched alkene with C4H8. Compare its connections with but-1-ene and but-2-ene; the central carbon has no hydrogen.

methanol.title: Methanol
methanol.alt: Displayed structure of Methanol. An unbranched alcohol with the -OH group at the end. Count all carbon atoms before choosing the name.
methanol.caption: An unbranched alcohol with the -OH group at the end. Count all carbon atoms before choosing the name.

propan-1-ol.title: Propan-1-ol
propan-1-ol.alt: Displayed structure of Propan-1-ol. An unbranched alcohol with the -OH group at the end. Count all carbon atoms before choosing the name.
propan-1-ol.caption: An unbranched alcohol with the -OH group at the end. Count all carbon atoms before choosing the name.

butan-1-ol.title: Butan-1-ol
butan-1-ol.alt: Displayed structure of Butan-1-ol. An unbranched alcohol with the -OH group at the end. Count all carbon atoms before choosing the name.
butan-1-ol.caption: An unbranched alcohol with the -OH group at the end. Count all carbon atoms before choosing the name.

methanoic-acid.title: Methanoic acid
methanoic-acid.alt: Displayed structure of Methanoic acid. The carboxyl carbon counts in the chain. One oxygen is double bonded; the other has an O–H bond.
methanoic-acid.caption: The carboxyl carbon counts in the chain. One oxygen is double bonded; the other has an O–H bond.

propanoic-acid.title: Propanoic acid
propanoic-acid.alt: Displayed structure of Propanoic acid. The carboxyl carbon counts in the chain. One oxygen is double bonded; the other has an O–H bond.
propanoic-acid.caption: The carboxyl carbon counts in the chain. One oxygen is double bonded; the other has an O–H bond.

butanoic-acid.title: Butanoic acid
butanoic-acid.alt: Displayed structure of Butanoic acid. The carboxyl carbon counts in the chain. One oxygen is double bonded; the other has an O–H bond.
butanoic-acid.caption: The carboxyl carbon counts in the chain. One oxygen is double bonded; the other has an O–H bond.

chloroethene.title: Chloroethene
chloroethene.alt: Displayed structure of Chloroethene. The chlorine is a side group on one alkene carbon. It remains attached to that carbon in poly(chloroethene).
chloroethene.caption: The chlorine is a side group on one alkene carbon. It remains attached to that carbon in poly(chloroethene).

tetrafluoroethene.title: Tetrafluoroethene
tetrafluoroethene.alt: Displayed structure of Tetrafluoroethene. All four hydrogen positions of ethene are replaced by fluorine in this monomer. The C=C becomes a single backbone bond on polymerisation.
tetrafluoroethene.caption: All four hydrogen positions of ethene are replaced by fluorine in this monomer. The C=C becomes a single backbone bond on polymerisation.

polypropene.title: Poly(propene) repeat unit
polypropene.alt: A two-carbon single-bonded backbone with side groups preserved from the corresponding alkene.
polypropene.caption: The bonds through the brackets continue into neighbouring repeat units. Restore C=C between these two backbone carbons to recover the monomer.

pvc.title: Poly(chloroethene) repeat unit
pvc.alt: A two-carbon single-bonded backbone with side groups preserved from the corresponding alkene.
pvc.caption: The bonds through the brackets continue into neighbouring repeat units. Restore C=C between these two backbone carbons to recover the monomer.

ptfe.title: Poly(tetrafluoroethene) repeat unit
ptfe.alt: A two-carbon single-bonded backbone with side groups preserved from the corresponding alkene.
ptfe.caption: The bonds through the brackets continue into neighbouring repeat units. Restore C=C between these two backbone carbons to recover the monomer.

ethanedioic-acid.title: Ethanedioic acid
ethanedioic-acid.alt: Displayed structure of Ethanedioic acid. There are two carboxyl groups and no intervening CH2 group. Both carboxyl carbons become part of the polyester backbone.
ethanedioic-acid.caption: There are two carboxyl groups and no intervening CH2 group. Both carboxyl carbons become part of the polyester backbone.

ethanediol.title: Ethane-1,2-diol
ethanediol.alt: Displayed structure of Ethane-1,2-diol. The two alcohol groups allow reaction at both ends. This is different from ethanol, which has just one -OH group.
ethanediol.caption: The two alcohol groups allow reaction at both ends. This is different from ethanol, which has just one -OH group.

plant-cell-detail.title: Plant cell: organelles in context
plant-cell-detail.alt: Cutaway plant cell showing cell wall, plasma membrane, chloroplasts, mitochondria, large vacuole and nucleus.
plant-cell-detail.caption: A teaching cutaway, not to scale. The cell wall lies outside the plasma membrane; the vacuole occupies much of the mature cell.

elements.text: Cytoplasm surrounds the organelles inside the membrane.

animal-cell-detail.title: Animal cell: a detailed internal view
animal-cell-detail.alt: Irregular animal cell outline with a nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, rough endoplasmic reticulum and ribosomes.
animal-cell-detail.caption: Cell shapes vary by function. This diagram highlights cellular structures without implying that every animal cell has this exact shape.

elements.text: No cellulose wall, chloroplasts or large permanent central vacuole.

leaf-detail.title: Leaf cross-section: routes for light, water and gases
leaf-detail.alt: Layered leaf section with cuticle, epidermis, palisade cells, spongy air spaces, vascular bundle and an open stoma.
leaf-detail.caption: An idealised cross-section. Palisade cells contain many chloroplasts; internal air spaces connect mesophyll surfaces with stomata.

elements.text: CO₂ enters; O₂ and water vapour can leave through the stomatal pore.

alveolus-detail.title: Alveolus and capillary: a short diffusion path
alveolus-detail.alt: Alveolar air space surrounded by a thin wall and a capillary containing red blood cells, with oxygen and carbon dioxide arrows.
alveolus-detail.caption: One alveolus is enlarged. Ventilation renews alveolar air and blood flow renews the capillary contents, maintaining diffusion gradients.

elements.text: Oxygen: air → blood. Carbon dioxide: blood → air.

heart-detail.title: Heart: chambers, valves and double circulation
heart-detail.alt: Cutaway schematic heart with separate right and left chambers, atrioventricular valves and labelled routes through lung and body circuits.
heart-detail.caption: The heart’s right side appears on the left of this view. Blue and red distinguish lower and higher oxygen content, not the actual colour of blood.

elements.text: Body → right heart → lungs → left heart → body. Septum separates the pumps.

nephron-detail.title: Nephron: filter, recover and regulate
nephron-detail.alt: Glomerulus inside Bowman’s capsule with a coiled proximal tubule, loop of Henle, distal tubule and collecting duct.
nephron-detail.caption: An idealised nephron, not to scale. Ultrafiltration occurs at the renal corpuscle; selective reabsorption returns useful substances to blood.

elements.text: Large proteins and blood cells remain in blood during normal ultrafiltration.

eye-detail.title: Eye cross-section: light and focusing
eye-detail.alt: Cross-section of an eye with cornea, iris, lens, retina, optic nerve and accommodation fibres.
eye-detail.caption: Light is refracted at the cornea and lens. The retina detects the image; the optic nerve carries impulses to the brain.

elements.text: Accommodation changes lens curvature; the pupil reflex changes the opening.

synapse-detail.title: Synapse: one-way chemical transmission
synapse-detail.alt: Presynaptic terminal with vesicles releasing neurotransmitter across a synaptic cleft onto postsynaptic receptors.
synapse-detail.caption: The gap is greatly enlarged. Neurotransmitter diffuses across the cleft and binds complementary receptors on the next cell.

elements.text: Release machinery and receptors on opposite sides make transmission directional.

enzyme-detail.title: Enzyme action and denaturation
enzyme-detail.alt: Three panels show substrate binding, products leaving an unchanged enzyme and an altered active site after denaturation.
enzyme-detail.caption: Shapes illustrate specificity, not literal molecular outlines. Denaturation alters the active site; it does not mean the enzyme has been used up.

elements.text: Low temperature usually slows collisions; excessive heat can denature the enzyme.

flower-detail.title: Flower structure and fertilisation route
flower-detail.alt: Longitudinal flower section showing stigma, style, ovary, ovules, anther and filament, with pollen tube route.
flower-detail.caption: Pollination delivers pollen to the stigma. Fertilisation occurs when a male nucleus reaches and fuses with the egg nucleus in an ovule.

elements.text: After fertilisation the ovule develops into a seed; the ovary develops into a fruit.

dna-detail.title: DNA: complementary bases and the double helix
dna-detail.alt: Two curved antiparallel backbones joined by complementary base pairs, with a magnified nucleotide key.
dna-detail.caption: Base pairing is A–T and C–G in DNA. The order of bases carries information; the base sequence is not the same on the complementary strand.

elements.text: one deoxyribose sugar and one base.
The backbone is sugar–phosphate; paired bases lie between the strands.

digestive-system-detail.title: Digestive system: processing and absorption
digestive-system-detail.alt: Digestive tract drawn from oesophagus to stomach, coiled small intestine and large intestine, with liver and pancreas.
digestive-system-detail.caption: Schematic position and relative size. Food travels through the gut; enzymes and bile enter it from associated organs.

elements.text: Bile is not an enzyme: it emulsifies fats and helps neutralise acidic chyme.

xylem-detail.title: Xylem and phloem: different transport pathways
xylem-detail.alt: Side-by-side longitudinal xylem vessel and phloem sieve tube with companion cells and directional flow arrows.
xylem-detail.caption: Xylem vessels are dead at maturity and conduct water and mineral ions; living phloem transports dissolved organic substances between sources and sinks.

elements.text: Phloem flow can occur in different directions in different tubes, not both in one arrow.

fermenter-detail.title: Industrial fermenter: controlled growth conditions
fermenter-detail.alt: Cutaway stirred tank with motor, agitators, cooling jacket, sterile air inlet, exhaust filter and sensor probes.
fermenter-detail.caption: A fermenter controls growth conditions. Air supply is suitable for aerobic processes; anaerobic fermentation uses a different oxygen regime.

elements.text: Sterile air inlet for an aerobic culture
Aseptic handling limits contamination; sensors support feedback control.

nitrogen-cycle-detail.title: Nitrogen cycle: identify each bacterial role
nitrogen-cycle-detail.alt: Nitrogen gas, ammonium, nitrite, nitrate and organic nitrogen connected by fixation, nitrification, assimilation, decomposition and denitrification.
nitrogen-cycle-detail.caption: Arrows track nitrogen-containing substances, not energy. Different microorganisms perform different conversions.

elements.text: Animals obtain nitrogen compounds by feeding; plants assimilate inorganic ions.

particle-states-detail.title: Particle model: solid, liquid and gas
particle-states-detail.alt: Three containers show particles closely packed in an ordered solid, close but irregular in a liquid and widely spaced in a gas.
particle-states-detail.caption: Particles retain their size when state changes. The drawings represent arrangement and movement; they do not show literal particle size.

elements.text: Heating raises average kinetic energy during a temperature rise, not during an ideal plateau.

ionic-dot-cross.title: Sodium chloride: transfer then electrostatic attraction
ionic-dot-cross.alt: Sodium ion with a positive charge and chloride ion with eight outer electrons, one marked as transferred from sodium.
ionic-dot-cross.caption: Only the chloride outer shell is shown. Dot and cross symbols show electron origins; electrons are otherwise identical.

elements.text: Attraction acts throughout a giant lattice

covalent-dot-cross.title: Water: bonding and lone pairs
covalent-dot-cross.alt: Oxygen and two hydrogen atoms with shared electron pairs and two lone pairs around oxygen.
covalent-dot-cross.caption: Each O–H shared pair contains one electron from hydrogen and one from oxygen. The model shows outer electrons, not literal orbital paths.

elements.text: Two bonds + two lone pairs around oxygen
This electron-accounting diagram does not imply a straight molecular geometry.

metallic-lattice.title: Metallic bonding and alloying
metallic-lattice.alt: Regular metal ions with delocalised electrons compared with an alloy whose different-sized atoms disrupt the layers.
metallic-lattice.caption: The dots represent delocalised electrons. Metallic attraction remains as layers move; differently sized atoms can hinder this movement.

elements.text: Positive ions are held together by electrostatic attraction to delocalised electrons.

distillation-detail.title: Simple distillation: separate and collect
distillation-detail.alt: Round-bottom flask, thermometer with bulb at side-arm height, sloping water-cooled condenser and open receiving flask.
distillation-detail.caption: Vapour enters the condenser and returns to liquid. Cooling water enters the lower connection and leaves at the upper connection; never seal a heated system.

elements.text: Choose fractional distillation when liquid boiling points need closer separation.

chromatography-detail.title: Paper chromatography: measure from the baseline
chromatography-detail.alt: Chromatography tank with solvent below a pencil baseline, separated spots and a marked solvent front with measurement arrows.
chromatography-detail.caption: Mark the solvent front promptly. Rf compares distances travelled from the same baseline and has no units.

elements.text: Use the same solvent, paper and conditions to compare Rf values.

titration-detail.title: Titration: controlled delivery and a clear endpoint
titration-detail.alt: Clamped burette over a conical flask on a white tile, with meniscus detail and a stopcock.
titration-detail.caption: Read the burette at eye level and use the bottom of the meniscus for a clear aqueous solution. The titre is final reading minus initial reading.

elements.text: Use concordant accurate titres; keep the rough titre out of the final mean.

electrolysis-detail.title: Electrolysis of aqueous copper(II) sulfate
electrolysis-detail.alt: Beaker with inert electrodes connected to a DC supply, copper ions moving to cathode and sulfate ions towards anode.
electrolysis-detail.caption: With inert electrodes, copper is deposited at the negative cathode and oxygen forms at the positive anode under the course conditions.

elements.text: Changing inert electrodes to copper electrodes changes the anode reaction.

energy-profile-detail.title: Energy profile: activation barrier and enthalpy
energy-profile-detail.alt: Smooth exothermic reaction profile with reactant and product energy levels and separate activation and energy-change arrows.
energy-profile-detail.caption: The vertical axis is energy and the horizontal axis is reaction progress, not time. A catalyst lowers activation energy without changing the start or finish energies.

elements.text: Bond breaking absorbs energy; bond formation releases energy.

fractionation-detail.title: Fractionating column: temperature and boiling ranges
fractionation-detail.alt: Industrial-style column with repeated trays and six collection levels, showing hot entry, rising vapour and cooler upper regions.
fractionation-detail.caption: Fractions are mixtures with boiling ranges. This is physical separation: molecules are not cracked by fractional distillation.

elements.text: Vapour rises and condenses where the temperature falls below its boiling range.

cuboid-section.title: 3D trigonometry: find the relevant triangle
cuboid-section.alt: Wireframe cuboid with a base diagonal, vertical rise and space diagonal highlighted as a right triangle.
cuboid-section.caption: The angle to the base is between the space diagonal and its projection onto the base. The pictorial drawing is not a scale diagram.

elements.text: Find the base diagonal first, then use triangle ACG for the requested angle.

cumulative-curve.title: Cumulative frequency: read quartiles from the total
cumulative-curve.alt: Increasing cumulative curve for forty observations with guides at cumulative frequencies ten, twenty and thirty.
cumulative-curve.caption: Example grouped distribution. Read across from n/4, n/2 and 3n/4, then down to the measurement axis; results are estimates.

elements.text: For 40 observations the quartile levels are 10, 20 and 30 on the vertical axis.

ray-detail.title: Refraction: angle to the normal, not the surface
ray-detail.alt: Incident and refracted rays crossing from air into glass, with a normal and marked incident and refracted angles.
ray-detail.caption: A ray slows and bends towards the normal on entering a higher-index medium. Frequency stays constant; wavelength decreases.

elements.text: Snell’s law for air to material: n = sin i / sin r, using angles from the normal.

sound-trace-detail.title: Oscilloscope: period and amplitude
sound-trace-detail.alt: Calibrated grid with a sinusoidal sound trace and arrows marking one period and amplitude from the centre line.
sound-trace-detail.caption: The vertical axis is detected signal and the horizontal axis is time. A whole cycle repeats the same phase, not just the next crossing.

elements.text: T = divisions per cycle × time per division. Convert to seconds before f = 1/T.

hr-detail.title: H–R diagram: luminosity and temperature
hr-detail.alt: Hertzsprung–Russell diagram with a descending main sequence, giants, supergiants and white dwarfs.
hr-detail.caption: This is a qualitative diagram, not an evolutionary track. Temperature decreases to the right; luminosity increases upwards.

motor-detail.title: Motor effect: current, field and force
motor-detail.alt: Magnet poles with field arrows from north to south and a current-carrying conductor marked out of the page with upward force.
motor-detail.caption: Conventional current is out of the page (dot), field is left to right, and force is upwards. Fleming’s left-hand rule gives the same result.

elements.text: Reverse current or field alone to reverse the force. Reversing both preserves it.

logic-detail.title: Combined Boolean circuit: (A AND B) OR NOT C
logic-detail.alt: Proper AND, NOT and OR gate outlines with wires and intermediate labels.
logic-detail.caption: Evaluate the intermediate AND and NOT outputs before the final OR. Wires convey logical values, not a choice of path.

elements.text: Example A=1, B=0, C=0: AND=0, NOT=1, so Q=1.

cpu-detail.title: Von Neumann architecture: registers and buses
cpu-detail.alt: CPU enclosure with control unit, ALU, program counter, MAR, MDR, CIR and accumulator alongside shared program/data memory.
cpu-detail.caption: A functional schematic, not a physical chip layout. Addresses identify locations; data and instructions are transferred as values.

elements.text: Fetch: PC address → MAR; memory value → MDR → CIR; PC advances as appropriate.

completed-square-graph.title: Completed square: a minimum above the axis
completed-square-graph.alt: Graph of y = (x + 3) squared plus 2, with vertex at minus three, two, no real roots and a symmetry line.
completed-square-graph.caption: This example has minimum y = 2 at x = −3. The curve cannot meet the x-axis, so the corresponding zero equation has no real solutions.

elements.text: The vertex is the midpoint in x of this symmetric example, and lies above y = 0.

tangent-gradient.title: Tangent gradient: instantaneous rate of change
tangent-gradient.alt: Curve y = x squared with a tangent at two, four and a gradient triangle using points one, zero and three, eight.
tangent-gradient.caption: The triangle is drawn on the tangent, not a chord of the curve. Here the tangent gradient is 8 ÷ 2 = 4.

elements.text: For a curved graph, estimate the tangent carefully and use a large gradient triangle.
